name: ZPM
desc:
Special hullmod that can be installed only when ZPM is present in inventory. Installation removes all installed Asgard hullmods.
Your fleet currently requires %s ZPMs to be operational, you have %s ZPMs in inventory.
If your number of ZPMs in inventory falls under %s, all ships loose equiped ZPM hullmods, connected boosts and will have to be re-equiped with ZPM hullmod again.

name: ZPM-Powered Shields
desc: ZPM overcharges shield systems to increased durability, arc and unfold speed.

name: ZPM-Powered Engines
desc: ZPM overcharges drive systems to increased speeds in hyperspace, star systems and battle.

name: ZPM-Powered Energy Weapons
desc: ZPM overcharges energy weapon systems to increased to increased damage, range and decreased flux cost.

name: ZPM-Flux System Bypass
desc: ZPM supplements ship systems, decreases supply consumption, and improves its flux stats.

name: #ASGARD MODS - MAKES SHIPS NOT BEING SHIT
Asgard Sensors
sModDesc: Increases the ship's in-combat vision range by %s/%s/%s/%s, based on hull size.

name: Asgard Computer Core
desc:
Increases the non-beam weapon range by %s, non-beam PD range by %s, and beam range by %s.
Can not work in conjunction with %s, %s, and other range related hullmods.
short: Increases weapon range, more so for larger ships.
sModDesc: Increases projectile speed by %s, as well as their distance traveled, past weapon range, by %s.

name: Asgard Shield
desc:
Rewires shield systems to absorb %s of damage taken as soft flux. Also extends the shield arc by %s degrees.
These modifications cause upkeep cost to increase by %s.
short: Lets shields absorb more soft flux on hit.
sModDesc: Shield emitters become %s more damage resistant. Converts front emitters to omni, or extends omni emitters by a further %s degrees.

name: Asgard hyperdrive
desc:
Increases maximum burn level by %s for frigates & destroyers, with an additional +1 for cruisers & capitals.
Restructure of the drive bubble reduces the impact of solar storms and other hazards by %s.
Hyperdrive emissions scale poorly with size, increasing cruiser & capital sensor profile by %s.
sModDesc: Further reduces solar and hyperspace hazardous impacts by %s.

name: Asgard Transporter
desc: Reduces the casualties suffered by fighter pilots by %s. Also lowers fighter refit time by %s, but uses up %s of the ship's flux capacity.
sModDesc: Separation of energy modules negates the flux capacity reduction.

name: Neutrino Ion Reactor
desc:
Lowers supply demands and fuel consumption by %s, thanks to the reactor's energy management systems.
Augments the ship’s flux capacity by %s and enhances dissipation by %s. Interfacing of the reactor-flux modules increases vent speed by %s, but causes the ship to take %s more EMP damage.
Equipment needed for the reactor both takes up %s of cargo space and results in %s slower ship repairs (in and out of combat).
short: A fragile reactor that reduces supply costs and increases flux stats.
sModDesc: Reduces armor by %s to accomodate for reactor integration.

name: Trinium Alloys
desc: Increases the ship's armor by %s/%s/%s/%s points, depending on hull size. Also increases EMP resistance by %s, due to the alloy's composition.
short: Increases armor, maneuverability, and EMP resistance.
sModDesc: Lightweight materials increase the ship's maneuverability by %s.

name: Naquadah Generators
desc:
Increases peak operating time of this ship by %s seconds.
Also reduces the rate at which combat readiness degrades by %s.

Upon destruction of the ship, generators on board will go critical, increasing ship explosion power by %s.
short: Increases peak time, CR degrades more slowly.
sModDesc: Integrated generators improve ship system reload times by %s.

name: Transport Rings
desc: Transportation rings deployment enhances ground support capabilities of up to %s marines on board. Medevac operations decrease causualities during raids by %s.
short: Gives bonuses to ground attack and reduces casualities.
sModDesc: Transport rings are integrated into logistics systems, reducing supply consumption per month by %s.
